## Natural history notes

A large carpenter ant characterized by a dark to reddish-brown body, long legs, elbowed antennae, and the robust build typical of Camponotus ants. In Florida, the Sandhill Carpenter Ant is found mainly in dry upland habitats such as sandhills, scrub, pine flatwoods, open pine-oak woods, and sandy forest edges where dead wood, roots, logs, or soil cavities provide nesting sites. Colonies forage for insects, honeydew, nectar, and scavenged material, helping move nutrients through sandy upland ecosystems while also serving as prey for birds, lizards, spiders, and other insect-eating animals.
